item.title: Saipan meeting cited in federal arms case
item.description: A RECENTLY unsealed federal case in the U.S. District Court for Utah details charges against a Chinese national, Ding Wei Chen, who is accused of conspiring to violate the Arms Export Control Act and smuggle defense articles from the United States. item.title: Citadel Pacific receives US congressional commendation
item.description: CITADEL Pacific last week received a commendation from U.S. Congresswoman Kimberlyn King-Hinds on behalf of the U.S. Congress “in recognition of its 20th anniversary and for fostering economic, environmental, and digital growth in support of local markets and networks in the CNMI.” The post Citadel Pacific receives US congressional commendation appeared first on Marianas Variety News & Views.

item.title: New law grants Legislature 273 days to establish financial system
item.description: GOVERNOR David M. Apatang on Monday approved House Bill 24-82, amending the revised fiscal year 2026 budget law to give the Legislature 273 days to establish its own financial system. The post New law grants Legislature 273 days to establish financial system appeared first on Marianas Variety News & Views.

item.title: Precinct 1 businessman urges lawmakers to disclose accomplishments
item.description: A PRECINCT 1 businessman and registered voter is calling on their six elected representatives to publicly disclose the legislation they have introduced and the accomplishments they have delivered since taking office, saying voters “deserve to see measurable results.” The post Precinct 1 businessman urges lawmakers to disclose accomplishments appeared first on Marianas Variety News & Views.

item.title: Saipan casino back in US news
item.description: THE controversies surrounding the islands’ casino industry have once again been brought to the attention of the nation’s capital by the Washington Post. The post Saipan casino back in US news appeared first on Marianas Variety News & Views.

item.title: 148,000 visitors projected for FY 2026
item.description: THE Marianas Visitors Authority is forecasting 148,000 visitors for fiscal year 2026, a slight improvement from earlier projections, but still below last year’s arrivals, as airlines continue to adjust flight schedules and seat capacity into the CNMI. The post 148,000 visitors projected for FY 2026 appeared first on Marianas Variety News & Views.

item.title: FY 2025 revenue surplus driven by one-time income amid tourism challenges
item.description: GOVERNOR David M. Apatang said the CNMI government ended fiscal year 2025 with a revenue surplus despite ongoing challenges in the tourism sector, attributing the “favorable variance” between projected and actual collections largely to one-time income sources, including Marianas Public Land Trust investment earnings and penalties collected from the bankrupt casino operator. The post FY 2025 revenue surplus driven by one-time income amid tourism challenges appeared first on Marianas Variety News
